Vessel tracks

Source: vignettes/articles/tracks.qmd

og_tracks() draws vessel tracks, a row a ping, for a quick look at what a step of their processing made of them: a time panel of speed under the map (a vessel chosen there, then one of its trips), lanes of what the vessel was doing and of its trips, the chosen span’s path and pings on the map, and the fishing effort by cell, which follows the vessel chosen. The processing is ramb’s: flags, harbours, trips, fishing and effort. ogis only draws, so a step’s output, ramb’s or another workflow’s, can be looked at as soon as it is made.

library(ogis)
library(dplyr)

Trips and effort

Two Danish small-scale vessels, a gillnetter and a trawler, a ping a minute: ramb flags the pings that cannot be right, finds those in a harbour, cuts the track into trips there (the ICES workshop’s rule, "jepol"), and gives each ping the hours it stands for.

h <- ramb::rb_read_example("dansk_harbours") |> collect()
harbours <- sf::st_sf(
  port_id = h$SI_HARB,
  geometry = sf::st_as_sfc(structure(h$geometry, class = "WKB"), crs = 4326)
)
pings <- ramb::rb_read_example("dansk") |>
  collect() |>
  filter(vessel_id %in% c("EX_6", "EX_12")) |>
  rename(vid = vessel_id, time = time_stamp) |>
  arrange(vid, time) |>
  group_by(vid) |>
  slice(seq(1, n(), by = 6)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ramb::rb_flag_ping_invalid() |>
  ramb::rb_flag_ping_impossible(method = "clean") |>
  filter(is.na(ping_flag)) |>
  ramb::rb_flag_ping_port(harbours)
pings <- pings |>
  ramb::rb_add_voyages(ramb::rb_create_voyages(pings, method = "jepol")) |>
  ramb::rb_add_effort()
og_tracks(pings, title = "Danish vessels")

What to look at:

  • The trips. Under Time, choose a vessel, then a trip: the map and the panel show that trip alone. The lane trip shows where each trip begins and ends against the speed: a trip should leave a harbour and come back to one. A trip is known by its vessel and ramb’s number for it, which starts again each year.
  • What the vessel was doing. The lane behaviour and the pings’ colours: fishing at slow, steady speed, steaming fast between.
  • The effort. Show follows the panel’s vessel: its own effort, its gear’s, or the whole fleet’s. Cells sets their size, live: about a pixel at each zoom, or 0.01 to 0.5 degrees at every zoom, a c-square (0.05) or an ICES rectangle (1 by 0.5), so the picture’s dependence on the grid is seen. Vessels, at least hides the cells of fewer vessels, as a confidentiality rule would; a click on a cell shows its number.

Flags against the truth

A flagging step is checked against faults known to be there. ramb’s dansk_planted is a vessel’s track with faults planted in it (a ping moved, its time shifted, …). The panel marks both, the planted faults and the pings ramb flags, each a row of ticks along the chart’s top and a ring on the map:

planted <- ramb::rb_read_example("dansk_planted") |>
  collect() |>
  filter(vid == first(vid)) |>
  arrange(time) |>
  ramb::rb_flag_ping_impossible(method = "clean")
count(planted, planted = !is.na(fault), flagged = !is.na(ping_flag))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   planted flagged     n
#>   <lgl>   <lgl>   <int>
#> 1 FALSE   FALSE    3746
#> 2 FALSE   TRUE       82
#> 3 TRUE    FALSE      54
#> 4 TRUE    TRUE       44
og_tracks(planted, activity = "fishing",
          marks = c(planted = "fault", flagged = "ping_flag"),
          effort = FALSE, title = "Planted faults")

The map opens on the whole track, a line across the Baltic among it: a ping moved a thousand kilometres east, as one of the planted faults does. A planted fault with no flag is one the step missed; a flag with no planted fault, a good ping it took for a bad one. Drag across the chart where they cluster, to see them on the map.

What an observer saw, against a rule

An observer’s labels, ping by ping, against what a rule infers from the track: here Malagasy small-scale gillnet trips (ramb’s ird_mg_gillnet). The observer’s labels say when the net was set or hauled; a speed rule says fishing where the boat is slow. compare holds the two against each other: each is a lane, and the panel marks the pings they give differently, a row of ticks along the chart’s top. The observer’s own labels are a lane too, and show their state (the same activity spelled three ways).

gillnet <- ramb::rb_read_example("ird_mg_gillnet") |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(
    rule = if_else(speed < 1.5, "fishing", "other"),
    observer = case_when(
      label %in% c("Pose_filet", "Remonter_filet",
                   "Remonter_filet_collecte") ~ "fishing",
      !is.na(label) ~ "other"
    )
  )
og_tracks(gillnet, activity = "rule", trip = "trip", lanes = c(label = "label"),
          compare = c(rule = "rule", observer = "observer"),
          effort = FALSE, title = "Gillnet trips")

Choose a trip and drag across a cluster of marks: the rule calls fishing where the boat drifts, or misses the net’s setting where the boat moves faster.

Another workflow’s output

og_tracks() finds its columns by name: ramb’s, or those of the EM4SSF project’s track format (D2.1: VESSEL_ID, DATE_TIME, LONGITUDE, LATITUDE, SPEED, TRIP_ID, ACTIVITY, GEAR), or those given. A file written by any step of such a workflow is looked at in one line, another method’s trips held against it:

og_tracks("trips_step01.parquet", compare = c(ramb = "trip_key", EM4SSF = "TRIP_ID"), effort = FALSE)

A set and its haul, drawn as a segment with a time (og_segment()), follow the panel as the pings do: a static gear’s soak is checked on the map beside the track that made it.
